rating_cap: RF-CAP-004 (serial-acquirer pattern, Critical materiality, management-governance module) caps the rating at Watchlist — no bypass regardless of thesis type or edge score, per Rating Cap Rules / eval check AD.
variant_perception_summary: The market's implied bar (14.7% FCFF growth, 12.8% terminal margin, per the reverse-DCF) sits below what Uber already delivers and below consensus, so the current -17.5% NTM EV/EBITDA peer discount is not fully explained by growth pessimism alone. The engine's edge is narrow (score 40/100, below the 50-point conviction-unlocking threshold): the Delivery Hero bridge facility's forward covenant compression (a 0.9%-25.5% EBITDA-decline breach threshold once drawn) is real and quantified but not yet visible in any currently reported balance-sheet ratio, and the ~10pp Gross-Bookings-to-Revenue gap remains genuinely unresolved against any primary filing.
what_everyone_knows: Uber is the largest global ride-hailing/delivery marketplace, has turned durably profitable, is buying back stock, and has signed a large, debt-funded, publicly known acquisition of Delivery Hero (announced 2026-07-16). Driver-classification regulatory risk and an AV-partnership (not owned-technology) strategy are widely discussed.
what_is_priced_in: A cautious growth/margin case: the reverse-DCF shows the $68.18 price requires only 14.7% FCFF growth and a 12.8% terminal margin, both below Uber's own consensus-anchored case (18.6%/16.0%) and below what Uber already delivers (12.1% LTM EBIT margin). The 'no moat proven' finding and the M&A/capital-allocation risk are likely already contributing to the -17.5% NTM EV/EBITDA discount to the core peer set.
what_market_may_be_missing: (1) The Delivery Hero bridge facility's forward covenant compression is not visible in any currently reported balance-sheet ratio because the debt has not been drawn yet. (2) SG&A leverage — the largest quantified earnings sensitivity — has already begun reversing (LTM ratio 20.50% vs. the FY2025 low of 19.87%) ahead of a headline miss. (3) The ~10pp Gross-Bookings-to-Revenue gap remains unreconciled against any primary filing; management's 'optical' explanation is unverified.
edge_proof: If the FQ3 2026 print (guided 2026-08-05, reported ~late Oct 2026) shows the LTM SG&A ratio continuing to rise past 20.50% AND reported Revenue growth continuing to lag Gross Bookings growth by a similar or wider gap with no primary-filing reconciliation offered, that confirms the margin/re-rating case is more fragile than the market's already-cautious bar assumes. Conversely, if the Delivery Hero bridge facility's actual covenant package (expected ahead of the H2 2027 close) shows real post-draw headroom, the balance-sheet risk this dossier flags is refuted.
killer_risk: The Delivery Hero acquisition closing and drawing its ~€14bn bridge facility without adequate disclosed covenant headroom — pro-forma leverage would compress the assumed covenant cushion from +62-72% today to a breach on as little as a 0.9%-25.5% EBITDA decline, turning an ordinary recession into a covenant crisis at the exact moment leverage discipline is least proven (RF-CAP-004).

earnings.verdict: Mixed earnings setup; red-flag severity: Material concerns

red_flags.description: Serial-acquirer pattern: at least 7 acquisitions in ~18 months culminating in the $14.8bn, debt-funded Delivery Hero deal (10.6% of Uber's own market cap), financed by a ~€14bn bridge facility, requiring a forced $1.6bn divestiture, and net debt jumping from $76mm to $9,340mm in one LTM window. Materiality-Critical per the module's own tagging; not one of the enumerated fraud/going-concern/enforcement/restatement/RPT>10% hard-lock triggers (module's own hard-lock Critical count = 0), but independently caps the master rating at Watchlist via the separate, non-bypassable CLAUDE.md §24 Filter 4 mechanism.

Recurring non-GAAP aggressiveness: ~25% of Adjusted EBITDA's own addback never itemized (FY2025 gap +38.3% vs GAAP-based EBITDA); a deferred-tax valuation-allowance release inflated GAAP net income by a combined $10,104mm over two consecutive years (FY2024 $5,758mm + FY2025 $4,346mm), never flagged as a distortion on any call in the pool.

Contingent-liability spike: total contingent exposure of at least $6,414mm (22.6% of Jun-30-2026 total equity), driven by a $5,611mm gross unrecognized tax benefit that grew 13.7% year-over-year and is not separately broken out from Other Non-Current Liabilities on the balance sheet, plus a live €700mm Delivery Hero termination fee and an active wrongful-death lawsuit.

Fast-changing industry / rate-of-change risk (≤40 threshold, scored 35/100): Uber is spreading ~$10bn across six-plus unproven AV partners rather than owning proprietary technology, and cannot predict who wins the AV transition. Non-binding on the actual business-quality score (47 already sits below the 65 cap) but flags this as a sector/technology-cycle bet, not a settled durable compounder.

Unreconciled ~10-percentage-point gap between Mobility Gross Bookings growth (+22% YoY) and reported Revenue growth (+12.2% YoY); management's 'optical, UK reclassification' explanation is unverified against any primary filing. Determines whether the earnings setup reads as genuinely accelerating or decelerating.

Once the Delivery Hero acquisition closes and the ~€14bn bridge facility is drawn, pro-forma leverage on mid-cycle EBITDA runs 5.0x-6.6x and an assumed 3.5x covenant would breach at an EBITDA decline of just 0.9% (full-bridge draw) to 25.5% (consideration-only) — a normal 30-40% recession breaches it in three of four pro-forma combinations modeled. Covenant terms themselves are undisclosed (Not assessable).
